microwave-assisted catalytic intermolecular hydroamination of alkynes is a fast reaction and that the regioselectivity of the addition of amineto terminal alkynes depends on the nature of the alkyne.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a new, fast, and convenient synthetic method for hydroamination reactions of alkynes.
the development of new methods for the catalytic addition of aminoboranes to alkynes and the subsequent hydrolytic cleavage of the resulting iminoborane to give the corresponding imines.
the development of new methods for the synthesis of secondary amines.

the microwave technology has a positive effect on all of the investigated reactions.
the hydroamination reactions of alkynes can be accelerated by use of microwave irradiation and that this technology can also be used for the preparation of terminal alkynes.
microwave-assisted hydroaminations of alkynes can be performed in high yields and short times.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
microwave irradiation of the reaction mixture results in a significant acceleration of hydroamination reactions and in a higher regioselectivity of the addition of aminos to terminal alkynes.

microwave-assisted reactions can provide a new dimension in the design and development of transition metal catalyzed reactions.
